TASK: carvana endpoints for searching for cars for sale given model, type, as many filters as possible; get features, data, price, and links

MANDATORY FIRST STEP: Review the routine documentation before doing anything else.
Call search_docs('operation') and get_doc_file on the Routine/operation model files
to understand ALL operation types (fetch, click, input_text, js_evaluate, download, etc.).
You CANNOT dispatch experiments until you understand the full routine capabilities.

After reviewing docs:
1. Analyze the exploration summaries
2. Call plan_routines to declare what routines to build
3. Use dispatch_experiments_batch to test ALL priority-1 routines IN PARALLEL
4. Record findings for each, then batch the next round
5. Build and submit_routine for each proven routine
6. Call mark_complete when all routines are shipped or failed

IMPORTANT: Always use dispatch_experiments_batch (not dispatch_experiment) to run multiple experiments in parallel. This is much faster.

      3,"> Fetch operations fail with \"TypeError: Failed to fetch\" when the browser's origin doesn't match the API server's CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header. Fix by adding a `navigate` operation to the allowed origin before any `fetch`. Related: [fetch.md](../operations/fetch.md), [navigation.md](../operations/navigation.md)"
      5,"**Symptom:** Fetch operation returns `TypeError: Failed to fetch` or the response data is `null`/empty despite the endpoint working in experiments."
      7,"**Root Cause:** The routine executor starts from `about:blank` (origin = `null`). Many APIs restrict CORS to their own website origin. For example, `api.nasdaq.com` only allows requests from origin `https://www.nasdaq.com`. Without a `navigate` operation first, the browser's origin is `null` and every `fetch` is blocked by CORS."
      9,"**How to detect:** If an experiment confirmed the API works from the site's origin (e.g. `browser_eval_js(fetch(...))` succeeded after navigating to `www.example.com`) but the routine's `fetch` operation fails with `TypeError: Failed to fetch`, the routine is missing a `navigate` step."
      19,"| All else fails | Use `js_evaluate` with `fetch()` instead of a `fetch` operation — JS fetch from the navigated page context has the correct origin |"
      21,"**RULE:** Every routine that calls an external API SHOULD start with a `navigate` operation to establish the correct browser origin. This is cheap (one page load) and prevents CORS issues."

content: "\"\"\"\nbluebox/data_models/routine/dev_routine.py\n\nThis primarily serves as an intermediate data model for routine discovery.\nThis data model is much simpler than the production routine data model,\nwhich makes it easier for the LLM agent to generate.\n\nKey differences from production Routine:\n- DevEndpoint has headers/body as strings (not dicts) - simpler for LLM\n- Only 4 operation types: navigate, sleep, fetch, return\n- No execution logic - just data validation\n\"\"\"\n\nimport re\nfrom typing import Literal\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\n\nfrom bluebox.data_models.routine.endpoint import HTTPMethod, CREDENTIALS\nfrom bluebox.data_models.routine.operation import RoutineOperationTypes\nfrom bluebox.data_models.routine.parameter import Parameter\n\n\nclass DevEndpoint(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"\n    Simplified endpoint model for LLM generation.\n    Headers and body are strings (not dicts) for easier generation.\n    \"\"\"\n    url: str\n    description: str | None = None\n    method: HTTPMethod\n    headers: str  # JSON string, not dict\n    body: str     # JSON string, not dict\n    credentials: CREDENTIALS = CREDENTIALS.SAME_ORIGIN\n\n\n# Dev operation classes - simple data models without execute() methods\n# Uses production RoutineOperationTypes enum for consistency\n\nclass DevNavigateOperation(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Navigate operation for dev routine (data-only, no execute).\"\"\"\n    type: Literal[RoutineOperationTypes.NAVIGATE] = RoutineOperationTypes.NAVIGATE\n    url: str\n\n\nclass DevSleepOperation(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Sleep operation for dev routine (data-only, no execute).\"\"\"\n    type: Literal[RoutineOperationTypes.SLEEP] = RoutineOperationTypes.SLEEP\n    timeout_seconds: float\n\n\nclass DevFetchOperation(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"\n    Fetch operation for dev routine (data-only, no execute).\n    Key difference: uses DevEndpoint (string headers/body) instead of Endpoint (dict).\n    \"\"\"\n    type: Literal[RoutineOperationTypes.FETCH] = RoutineOperationTypes.FETCH\n    endpoint: DevEndpoint\n    session_storage_key: str\n\n\nclass DevReturnOperation(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Return operation for dev routine (data-only, no execute).\"\"\"\n    type: Literal[RoutineOperationTypes.RETURN] = RoutineOperationTypes.RETURN\n    session_storage_key: str\n\n\n# Dev routine operation union\nDevOperationUnion = DevNavigateOperation | DevSleepOperation | DevFetchOperation | DevReturnOperation\n\n\nclass DevRoutine(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"\n    Simplified routine model for LLM generation during discovery.\n    \"\"\"\n    name: str\n    description: str\n    operations: list[DevOperationUnion]\n    parameters: list[Parameter]\n    \n    def validate(self) -> tuple[bool, list[str], Exception | None]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Validate the dev routine structure.\n        \n        Returns:\n            tuple containing:\n                - result: True if valid, False otherwise\n                - errors: List of error messages\n                - exception: Exception if one occurred\n        \"\"\"\n        result = True\n        errors = []\n        exception = None\n        \n        try: \n            # Must have at least 3 operations (navigate, fetch, return)\n            if len(self.operations) < 3:\n                result = False\n                errors.append(\"Must have at least 3 operations (navigate, fetch, return)\")\n            \n            # First operation should be navigate\n            if not isinstance(self.operations[0], DevNavigateOperation):\n                result = False\n                errors.append(\"First operation should be a navigate operation\")\n                \n            # Last operation should be return\n            if not isinstance(self.operations[-1], DevReturnOperation):\n                result = False\n                errors.append(\"Last operation should be a return operation\")\n                \n            # Second to last should be fetch\n            if not isinstance(self.operations[-2], DevFetchOperation):\n                result = False\n                errors.append(\"Second to last operation should be a fetch operation\")\n                \n            # Get all placeholders\n            all_placeholders = set(self._get_all_placeholders(self.model_dump_json()))\n                \n            # Check that every parameter is used\n            defined_parameters = {p.name for p in self.parameters}\n            unused_parameters = defined_parameters - all_placeholders\n            if unused_parameters:\n                result = False\n                for param_name in unused_parameters:\n                    errors.append(f\"Parameter '{param_name}' is not used in the routine operations\")\n            \n            # Remaining placeholders (not parameters)\n            remaining_placeholders = all_placeholders - defined_parameters\n                    \n            # All remaining placeholders should be valid prefixes\n            valid_prefixes = [\"sessionStorage\", \"cookie\", \"localStorage\", \"uuid\", \"epoch_milliseconds\", \"meta\", \"windowProperty\"]\n            for placeholder in remaining_placeholders:\n                prefix = placeholder.split(\":\")[0]\n                if prefix not in valid_prefixes:\n                    result = False\n                    errors.append(f\"Placeholder '{placeholder}' has invalid prefix. Valid: {valid_prefixes}\")\n                        \n            # Get used session storage keys from placeholders\n            used_session_storage_keys = set()\n            for placeholder in all_placeholders:\n                if placeholder.split(\":\")[0] == \"sessionStorage\":\n                    used_session_storage_keys.add(placeholder.split(\":\")[1].split(\".\")[0])\n            \n            # Include return operation's key\n            if isinstance(self.operations[-1], DevReturnOperation):\n                used_session_storage_keys.add(self.operations[-1].session_storage_key)\n                    \n            # Get all fetch session storage keys\n            all_fetch_keys = set()\n            for operation in self.operations:\n                if isinstance(operation, DevFetchOperation):\n                    all_fetch_keys.add(operation.session_storage_key)\n            \n            # Check unused fetch keys\n            unused_keys = all_fetch_keys - used_session_storage_keys\n            if unused_keys:\n                result = False\n                for key in unused_keys:\n                    errors.append(f\"Fetch session storage key '{key}' is not used\")\n                    \n            # Last fetch key should match return key\n            if len(self.operations) >= 3:\n                if isinstance(self.operations[-1], DevReturnOperation) and isinstance(self.operations[-2], DevFetchOperation):\n                    if self.operations[-1].session_storage_key != self.operations[-2].session_storage_key:\n                        result = False\n                        errors.append(\"Last fetch session_storage_key should match return session_storage_key\")\n            \n        except Exception as e:\n            result = False\n            errors.append(f\"Exception: {e}\")\n            exception = e\n            \n        return result, errors, exception\n    \n    def _get_all_placeholders(self, routine_string: str) -> list[str]:\n        \"\"\"\n        Extract all placeholders {{...}} from routine string.\n        \"\"\"\n        placeholders = re.findall(r'{{.*?}}', routine_string)\n        return [placeholder[2:-2] for placeholder in set(placeholders)]""

arguments.usage_guide:
There are two shipped Carvana routines:

1) carvana_search_inventory
   - What it does: Navigates to the public Carvana /cars search results page, performs a keyword search in the built-in search box, and scrapes structured Vehicle ld+json blobs for all vehicles currently shown.
   - Inputs: `search_query` (string) — a keyword such as a make, model, or general term (e.g., "audi", "tesla", "suv").
   - Output: An object with `count` and `vehicles[]`, where each vehicle includes name, model year, VIN, SKU, mileageFromOdometer, an `offers` object (price, priceCurrency, availability, canonical vehicle URL), and a top-level `url` pointing to the VDP.
   - When to use: Whenever you need to find cars for sale on Carvana by free-text search and get a list of matching vehicles with VINs, prices, and links, without touching Carvana’s internal APIs. Use this first to discover interesting vehicles and capture their `vehicleId` from the URL.

2) carvana_get_vehicle_details
   - What it does: Navigates directly to a specific Carvana vehicle details page (VDP) using a known `vehicleId` and extracts rich structured data from `window.__NEXT_DATA__.props.pageProps.forProviders.forVehicleContext.vehicleDetails`.
   - Inputs: `vehicle_id` (integer) — the Carvana internal ID from the VDP URL path `/vehicle/{vehicleId}`. Obtain it from `carvana_search_inventory` results (parse the numeric ID from each `url`) or by copying from a VDP URL.
   - Output: A structured object with core identity fields (vehicleId, VIN, SKU, year, make, model, trim), usage info (mileage), pricing (price, priceCurrency, MSRP), inventory metadata (inventoryType), main image URL, canonical URL, and a `raw` sub-object containing many additional specs, features, warranty, location, and media details.
   - When to use: After you know exactly which Carvana vehicle you care about and need deep details beyond what the SRP exposes.

How to use them together:
- Step 1: Call `carvana_search_inventory` with an appropriate `search_query` (e.g., a make+model) to get a list of matching vehicles. Inspect the returned `vehicles` array and pick one or more candidates by their `url`.
- Step 2: Extract the numeric `vehicleId` from each chosen `url` (it’s the path segment after `/vehicle/`).
- Step 3: For each chosen ID, call `carvana_get_vehicle_details` with `vehicle_id` to retrieve a comprehensive details payload suitable for downstream analysis, comparison, or display.

Notes:
- Both routines work entirely via public HTML/JS scraping, so they avoid Cloudflare-blocked internal APIs.
- Neither routine currently parameterizes advanced filters (price range, drivetrain, etc.); to approximate those, encode them into your `search_query` (e.g., "audi q8"), then post-filter the returned results client-side.
- If a given `vehicle_id` is invalid or no longer available, `carvana_get_vehicle_details` will return an error field like `vehicle_details_missing` from its js_evaluate step; callers should be prepared to handle null/empty results.
